title: My Best Friend Sold My PS5

beats.text: My best friend sold my PlayStation five for two hundred dollars. He said I should thank him.
beats.label: HE SOLD MY PS5

beats.text: I came home to cables hanging from an empty shelf. Ryan was counting money on my couch.
beats.label: EMPTY. SHELF.

beats.text: He said we needed cash for his birthday trip. Apparently, my console was our emergency fund.
beats.label: HIS BIRTHDAY TRIP

beats.text: I messaged the buyer. Before I could explain, he sent a photo of the console and one question.
beats.label: THE BUYER MESSAGED ME

beats.text: Why does this have a broken sticker? I zoomed in. That was the empty display shell from my repair project.
beats.label: WAIT. ZOOM IN.

beats.text: My real console was at my brother's place. I told the buyer the truth. Ryan had to return every dollar.
beats.label: AN EMPTY DISPLAY SHELL

beats.text: Then Ryan asked if the trip was still happening. I said yes. The buyer was taking him to the refund machine.
beats.label: TRIP TO THE REFUND MACHINE

title: My Roommate Charged Me for My Own WiFi

beats.text: My roommate charged me twenty dollars to use the WiFi. There was one tiny problem with his business plan.
beats.label: PAY TO CONNECT?

beats.text: The router was mine. The internet account was mine. Even the little table under the router was mine.
beats.label: ALL OF IT WAS MINE

beats.text: He said the fee covered network management. His entire job was telling guests to restart their phones.
beats.label: NETWORK MANAGER

beats.text: So I asked for an invoice. He made one in thirty seconds and added a five dollar administration fee.
beats.label: AN EXTRA FIVE DOLLARS

beats.text: I opened my provider account and paused his device. He immediately asked why the internet had stopped working.
beats.label: DEVICE PAUSED

beats.text: I told him to contact his network manager. For the first time all week, he had absolutely nothing to say.
beats.label: CONTACT YOUR MANAGER

beats.text: He refunded the money. I restored his connection and renamed the network: administration fee not included.
beats.label: REFUND COMPLETE

title: My Brother Sold My Concert Ticket

beats.text: My brother sold my concert ticket and told me the show was canceled. Then he forgot to hide his story.
beats.label: SHOW CANCELED?

beats.text: There he was, posting a photo outside the venue. His caption said best night ever. Very convincing cancellation.
beats.label: BEST NIGHT EVER

beats.text: I called him. He said the ticket would have gone to waste because I always arrived late anyway.
beats.label: HIS EXCUSE

beats.text: Then his buyer messaged me. My name was still on the ticket, and the transfer had never been completed.
beats.label: TRANSFER INCOMPLETE

beats.text: I explained what happened. The buyer asked my brother for a refund. I took back the unfinished transfer.
beats.label: THE ACTUAL OWNER

beats.text: I went to the concert with my friend. My brother stayed outside, arguing about a service fee he had invented.
beats.label: GUESS WHO GOT IN

beats.text: After the show, he asked for a ride home. I told him my taxi service had been canceled.
beats.label: SERVICE CANCELED

title: My Neighbor Returned an Empty Box

beats.text: My neighbor returned the drill I lent him. The box was suspiciously light. He said that was a premium feature.
beats.label: PREMIUM AIR?

beats.text: I opened it right in front of him. Inside were a receipt, a screwdriver, and absolutely no drill.
beats.label: ONE THING MISSING

beats.text: He said he must have mixed up the boxes. Then his phone rang. The screen said drill buyer.
beats.label: DRILL BUYER CALLING

beats.text: We stood there listening to the ringtone. He slowly turned the phone over as if that would erase my eyesight.
beats.label: AWKWARD SILENCE

beats.text: I asked him to call the buyer back. On speaker. The buyer had not collected it yet and agreed to cancel.
beats.label: PUT IT ON SPEAKER

beats.text: Ten minutes later, my drill came back from his garage. Apparently, that was where premium air was manufactured.
beats.label: FOUND IN HIS GARAGE

beats.text: He asked to borrow it next week. I handed him the screwdriver. That one was already in the box.
beats.label: BORROWING DOWNGRADED

title: My Friend Faked a Surprise Party

beats.text: My friend collected money for my surprise birthday party. The surprise was that nobody had booked a party.
beats.label: SURPRISE: NO PARTY

beats.text: Six friends showed up at an empty cafe. The owner looked at our balloons and asked who we were.
beats.label: NO RESERVATION

beats.text: Our organizer said the booking system had crashed. Unfortunately for him, the owner was holding the paper booking diary.
beats.label: A PAPER SYSTEM

beats.text: I asked where our money went. He said decorations. We counted two balloons and a napkin that said happy Tuesday.
beats.label: HAPPY TUESDAY?

beats.text: Then his delivery arrived. Brand new headphones. He had accidentally used the cafe address when placing the order.
beats.label: SPECIAL DELIVERY

beats.text: He refunded everyone and canceled his order. The owner let us push two tables together and brought out a cake.
beats.label: AN ACTUAL PARTY

beats.text: We still gave him a party job. He had to blow up every balloon. No budget required. Just hot air.
beats.label: FINALLY, HIS SPECIALTY
